page: OVHcloud r3-128 is a memory-optimized cloud instance provisioned on the KVM hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor running at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. It delivers 16 dedicated physical CPU cores with one thread per core, backed by 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and a 32 MB L3 cache. Compute capabilities include hardware support for AES, SHA-NI, AVX, and AMD SVM virtualization extensions, though AVX-512 and AMX instructions are absent.

Resource allocation is balanced specifically for memory-dense processing, offering 128 GB of system RAM at an allocation ratio of 8 GB per vCPU. Storage is locally attached via a bundled 400 GB NVMe SSD, providing low-latency disk access directly on the host. Network throughput is provisioned with a 4 Gbps baseline, and the instance includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Acceleration hardware is not present, with zero GPUs included.

Benchmark results reflect robust memory subsystems and consistent single-threaded execution. The instance scores in the top tier for PassMark memory performance and achieves strong uncached memory read and write bandwidths of 223.45 GB/sec and 117.55 GB/sec, respectively. In compute testing, stress-ng single-core performance registers in the top quartile, while multi-threaded stress-ng, Geekbench scores, and PassMark overall CPU metrics place squarely within the median range. Compression workloads display solid throughput, led by multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 215.99 GB/sec.

Given its dedicated core allocation, substantial memory density, and local NVMe storage, the r3-128 offers practical resource efficiency for in-memory caching layers such as Redis, relational and non-relational database engines, data transformation pipelines, and medium-scale analytics workloads that prioritize memory capacity over extreme multi-threaded CPU throughput.
